items.title: feat(iOS): map Apple billing plan products (installmentsInfo) to the hybrid SDKs
items.body:
### Summary

Maps Apple's monthly billing plans with a commitment (`StoreProduct.installmentsInfo`, purchases-ios 5.76.0+) through the iOS bridge so hybrid SDKs can display and purchase them. Closes #1793.

Today the native support stops at the bridge: `rc_dictionary` never reads `installmentsInfo`, the product's `identifier` is the base StoreKit id, and `CommonFunctionality.product(with:)` cannot resolve a `{productId}:monthly` identifier. So an app rendering its own paywall from React Native or Capacitor cannot show the two amounts Apple requires before purchase (the monthly billing price and the total commitment), cannot tell a commitment product apart from the upfront product backed by the same StoreKit product, and gets `Couldn't find product.` from `purchaseStoreProduct`.

### Changes

**iOS (`StoreProduct+HybridAdditions.swift`)**
- `installmentsInfo`: new key, `null` unless the product represents a billing plan. Carries the iOS `InstallmentsInfo` fields (`commitmentInstallmentsCount`, `commitmentInstallmentPeriod`, `installmentBillingPrice`, `installmentBillingDisplayPrice`, `commitmentTotalPeriod`, `commitmentTotalPrice`, `commitmentTotalDisplayPrice`, `billingPlanType`). Periods use the same `{unit, value, iso8601}` shape Android emits for `Period`.
- `productPlanIdentifier`: new key (`"monthly"` for a billing plan product, `null` otherwise), the same key the `EntitlementInfo` and `SubscriptionInfo` mappers already emit, so a product can be joined to the entitlement it unlocks.
- `identifier`: now the compound identifier purchases-ios resolves the product by, `{productIdentifier}:{productPlanIdentifier}` for a billing plan product. Unchanged for every other product. This matches Android, where `identifier` is already `StoreProduct.id` (`{productId}:{basePlanId}`). `StoreProduct.id` is internal to purchases-ios, so the bridge rebuilds it from `productIdentifier` and `billingPlanType.rawValue`, mirroring `BillingPlanType.compoundProductIDPlanComponent` (`upFront` has no plan component).

**iOS (`CommonFunctionality.swift`)**
- `product(with:)` matches on the compound identifier. purchases-ios already resolves `annual:monthly` in `getProducts`, but the result's `productIdentifier` is `annual`, so the old filter dropped it and every purchase by product identifier failed for billing plan products. Package purchases were unaffected.

**TypeScript (`@revenuecat/purchases-typescript-internal`)**
- `PurchasesStoreProduct.productPlanIdentifier: string | null` and `PurchasesStoreProduct.installmentsInfo: BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo | null`, plus the `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo` interface and `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE` enum. The existing `InstallmentsInfo` on `SubscriptionOption` keeps Google Play's shape untouched. API report regenerated.

**Android and Web mappers**
- Emit `productPlanIdentifier: null` and `installmentsInfo: null` on the product, following the existing convention for the other platform's fields (`discounts` on Android, the `pricePer*` fields on iOS).

### Compatibility

- Purely additive for every product that is not a billing plan: `identifier` is unchanged, the two new keys are `null`.
- Billing plan products need purchases-ios 5.76.0+ (already the pinned 5.90.1), iOS 26.4+, StoreKit 2, and a build with Xcode 26.5+; on anything older `installmentsInfo` stays `null` exactly as `StoreProduct.installmentsInfo` does natively.
- No new source files, so no `project.pbxproj` change.

### Tests

- `StoreProduct+HybridAdditionsTests`: `null` fields and unchanged identifier for a plain product, updated key count, and a billing plan product mapped through `TestStoreProduct(installmentsInfo:)` covering the compound identifier, `productPlanIdentifier`, every `installmentsInfo` field, and the `upFront` case.
- `CommonFunctionality+PurchaseTests`: purchasing by `annual:monthly` resolves the billing plan product and reaches `purchase(product:)`. This test fails on `main`.
- The billing plan tests register only on an iOS 26.4+ runtime, since `StoreProduct.installmentsInfo` is unavailable below it.
- Android `StoreProductMapperTests`: key count and the two `null` entries.
- Web `offerings_mapper.test.ts`: the two `null` entries.

Run locally: TypeScript lint/test/build/api-extractor, web lint/test, Android `StoreProductMapperTests`, and the two iOS suites above on an iOS 26.5 simulator.

Also exercised end to end from a React Native app (react-native-purchases 10.10.0 with this branch swapped in by path, Xcode 27, iOS 26.5 simulator, StoreKit configuration file declaring a `MONTHLY` billing plan): `getProducts(['annual:monthly', 'annual'])` returned both products with the plan product carrying `identifier: "annual:monthly"`, `productPlanIdentifier: "monthly"` and a full `installmentsInfo`, and `purchaseStoreProduct` on it reached StoreKit with RevenueCat logging `Applying billing plan of type monthly to the purchase` (it failed with `Couldn't find product.` before the lookup fix).

### Naming

Open to renaming `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo` / `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE` or moving `installmentsInfo` under a different key if you would rather keep the Google `InstallmentsInfo` name free for a future unification; the wire shape is the part that matters for the hybrid SDKs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes product `identifier` semantics for iOS billing-plan SKUs and purchase lookup; purchase flows and paywalls keyed on the old base id could break for those products, though plain products stay unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Exposes **Apple billing plan products** (monthly billing with commitment, iOS 26.4+) through the hybrid bridge so React Native and similar SDKs can show required pricing and purchase by the right id.
> 
> On **iOS**, `StoreProduct` wire maps now emit **`productPlanIdentifier`** and **`installmentsInfo`** (commitment counts, periods, display prices, `billingPlanType`), and **`identifier`** becomes the compound id (`annual:monthly`) for plan products—aligned with Android’s `{productId}:{basePlanId}` shape. **`CommonFunctionality.product(with:)`** resolves products using that compound id so `purchaseStoreProduct` no longer fails with “Couldn't find product.” when the native `productIdentifier` is only the base StoreKit id.
> 
> **TypeScript** adds `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo`, `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE`, and the new fields on `PurchasesStoreProduct` (API report updated). **Android** and **Web** mappers always send `productPlanIdentifier: null` and `installmentsInfo: null` for parity. Tests cover mapping, compound-id purchase, and null stubs on non-iOS platforms.
>

items.title: Release/5.0.0
items.body:
**RevenueCat Purchases Hybrid Common v5** is here!! 😻

This latest release updates the Android SDK dependency from v5 to [v6](https://github.com/RevenueCat/purchases-android/releases/tag/6.0.0) to use BillingClient 5. This version of BillingClient brings an entire new subscription model which has resulted in large changes across the entire SDK.

### Migration Guides
- See [Android Native - 5.x to 6.x Migration](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/android-native-5x-to-6x-migration) for a more thorough explanation of the new Google subscription model announced with BillingClient 5 and how to take advantage of it in V6. This guide includes tips on product setup with the new model.

### New `SubscriptionOption` concept

#### Purchasing
In v4, a Google Play Android `Package` or `StoreProduct` represented a single purchaseable entity, and free trials or intro offers would automatically be applied to the purchase if the user was eligible.

Now, in Hybrid Common v5, an Google Play Android `Package` or `StoreProduct` represents a duration of a subscription and contains all the ways to purchase that duration -- any offers and its base plan. Each of these purchase options are `SubscriptionOption`s.
When passing a `Package` to `purchasePackage()` or `StoreProduct` to `purchaseStoreProduct()`, the SDK will use the following logic to choose which `SubscriptionOption` to purchase:
- Filters out offers with "rc-ignore-offer" tag
- Uses `SubscriptionOption` with the longest free trial or cheapest first phase
    - Only offers the user is eligible will be applied
- Falls back to base plan

For more control, purchase subscription options with the new `purchaseSubscriptionOption()` method.

#### Models

`StoreProduct` now has a few new properties use for Google Play Android:
- `defaultOption`
  - A subscription option that will automatically be applie when purchasing a `Package` or `StoreProduct`
- `subscriptionOptions`
  - A list of subscription options (could be null)

##### Subscription Option

Below is an example of what a subscription option:

```js
{
    "id": "basePlan",
    "storeProductId": "subId:basePlanId",
    "productId": "subId",
    "pricingPhases": [
        {
            "price": 0,
            "priceString": "FREE",
            "period": "P1M",
            "cycles": 1
        },
        {
            "price": 4.99,
            "priceString": "$4.99",
            "period": "P1M",
            "cycles": 0
        }
    ],
    "tags": ["free-offers"],
    "isBasePlan": false,
    "billingPeriod": {
        "periodUnit": "MONTH",
        "periodNumberOfUnits": 0
    },
    "isPrepaid": false,
    "fullPricePhase": {
        "price": 4.99,
        "priceString": "$4.99",
        "period": "P1M",
        "cycles": 0
    },
    "freePhase" {
        "price": 0,
        "priceString": "FREE",
        "period": "P1M",
        "cycles": 1
    },
    "introPhase": null
}
```

### Observer Mode

Observer mode is still supported in v5. Other than updating the SDK version, there are no changes required.

### Offline Entitlements

✨ With this new feature, even if our main and backup servers are down, the SDK can continue to process purchases. This is enabled transparently to the user, and when the servers come back online, the SDK automatically syncs the information so it can be visible in the dashboard.

### Offering Metadata

✨ Metadata allows attaching arbitrary information as key/value pairs to your Offering to control how to display your products inside your app. The metadata you configure in an Offering is available from the RevenueCat SDK. For example, you could use it to remotely configure strings on your paywall, or even URLs of images shown on the paywall.

See the [metadata documentation](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/offering-metadata) for more info!

items.title: feat: add getOffering to fetch a single offering by identifier
items.body:
## What

Adds `getOffering(identifier)` to the iOS, Android and JS common layers. It returns the mapped dictionary for a single offering, or null when the identifier does not exist.

It calls the same `getOfferings()` on the underlying SDK as `getCurrentOfferingForPlacement` does, then maps one `Offering` instead of the whole `Offerings`. No new network call, no cache change, nothing existing is modified.

On which offering it returns: `Offerings.current` is not the same object as `Offerings.all[identifier]`. On iOS `current` is computed as `all[currentOfferingID]?.copyWith(targeting:)`, and on Android the parser builds it with `withPresentedContext(null, targeting)`. Only `current` carries the targeting context on its packages. So `getOffering` returns `current` when the caller asks for the current offering, and `all[identifier]` otherwise. That way a purchase made from the result still posts its applied targeting rule, and experiment attribution is not lost.

I got this wrong in the first version of this PR and the second commit fixes it. The tests in the first version could not catch it, so they were rewritten too.

## Why

Hybrid SDKs have no way to ask for one offering. An app that shows a single paywall still has to call `getOfferings()` and marshal every offering and every product across the bridge.

The native SDK is not the slow part. On an iPhone 13 Pro, in a React Native app with 33 offerings and 80 products, `getOfferings()` takes 330 to 370 ms measured from JS even when the native log says `Vending Offerings from memory cache`. There is no network and no StoreKit work in that number. It is the cost of building the dictionary and serializing it over the bridge, and an app that shows paywalls on several screens pays it on every screen.

Mapping one offering instead of 33 removes most of that. To be precise about the scope: this does not change what gets fetched. The full offerings response and the full product fetch still happen. What it removes is the dictionary construction and the bridge crossing for the offerings the caller did not ask for.

Related: RevenueCat/react-native-purchases#755

## Tests

Each of these fails against the first commit and passes against the second, so they are checking the thing that actually broke.

- iOS: new unit tests in `PurchasesHybridCommonTests`, the target the `test-ios-*` jobs run. Those jobs need no secret, unlike `integration-test-ios`, which only works after `replace_api_key_integration_tests` injects `REVENUECAT_API_KEY`. Because `Offerings.current` is computed as `all[currentOfferingID]?.copyWith(targeting:)`, passing a targeting value to the initialiser reproduces the real asymmetry through the real code path rather than hand-building the two payloads.
- iOS, integration: kept and strengthened. It compares `getOffering(currentIdentifier)` against the whole `getOfferings()["current"]` payload and checks every non-current offering against its `all` entry, so the behaviour is still verified against a real backend response when you run it. Plus an entry in the ObjC API tester.
- Android: new `CommonKtGetOfferingTests` with offerings shaped the way `OfferingParser` shapes them, so `current` and `all[identifier]` differ. There was no behavioural coverage of this area before. Plus Kotlin and Java API tests.
- JS: the fixture now gives `current` a targeting context that `all` does not have, so a test that reads the wrong one fails.
- Regenerated the `purchases-js-hybrid-mappings` API report.

CircleCI does not build pull requests from forks on this project, so none of these run here. I ran them all locally instead and reported the exact output below. `swift build`; the full `PurchasesHybridCommon` scheme on an iPhone 16 simulator (136 tests, 0 failures); `swiftlint` (violation counts identical to the base commit, file by file, and the new test file is clean); `./gradlew lint test detekt :api-tests:test`; and `yarn allchecks` in `purchases-js-hybrid-mappings`.

## One open question

On web I kept the full `getOfferings()` and sliced afterwards, so the JS path matches the native semantics exactly. purchases-js also has `getOfferings({ offeringIdentifier })`, which filters before fetching products and would be a real payload saving. I did not use it because it changes what ends up in `offeringsCache` and how `current` resolves when the requested offering is not the current one, and I would rather you decide that than guess. Happy to switch if you prefer it.

## Follow up

If this lands I would like to add the matching bridge method and TypeScript wrapper in react-native-purchases.

---

I cannot set labels on this repo. Per AGENTS.md this one should be `pr:feat`.

---

> **Medium Risk**
> New public hybrid API with subtle semantics around current vs catalog offerings; incorrect choice would drop targeting on purchases, though behavior is heavily tested and mirrors existing getOfferings mapping.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`getOffering(offeringIdentifier)`** across Android (`common.kt`), iOS (`CommonFunctionality`), and JS (`PurchasesCommon`) so hybrid apps can fetch one mapped offering (or `null`) instead of marshaling the full `getOfferings()` payload over the bridge.
> 
> Each implementation still calls the underlying **`getOfferings()`** (no new network or cache behavior) and maps a single offering. When the requested ID is the **current** offering, it returns **`Offerings.current`** rather than the catalog entry in `all`, so package **`presentedOfferingContext`** (including **targeting context**) matches what purchases need for experiment attribution.
>

items.title: feat(iOS): expose installment infos on StoreProduct for iOS
items.body:
Exposes `InstallmentsInfos` via PHC on `StoreProduct` for iOS 12mo commitment products.

### InstallmentsInfo Mapping
Here's how we're mapping `InstallmentsInfo` from iOS over to PHC:

| iOS `InstallmentsInfo` | PHC `InstallmentsInfo` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `commitmentInstallmentsCount: Int` | `commitmentPaymentsCount: Int` | Same thing, but different name. |
| `commitmentInstallmentsCount: Int` | `renewalCommitmentPaymentsCount: Int` | iOS doesn't have `renewalCommitmentPaymentsCount`, but they always renew for the same number of periods on iOS, so we can safely assign it to `commitmentInstallmentsCount`  |
| `commitmentInstallmentPeriod: SubscriptionPeriod` | `commitmentInstallmentPeriod: String` (ISO 8601, e.g. `"P1M"`) | New. `null` for Android. |
| `installmentBillingPrice: Decimal` | `installmentBillingPrice: Decimal` | New. `null` for Android. |
| `installmentBillingDisplayPrice: String` | `installmentBillingPriceString: String` | New. `null` for Android. |
| `commitmentTotalPeriod: SubscriptionPeriod` | `commitmentTotalPeriod: String` (ISO 8601, e.g. `"P1Y"`) | New. `null` for Android. |
| `commitmentTotalPrice: Decimal` | `commitmentTotalPrice: Decimal` | New. `null` for Android. |
| `commitmentTotalDisplayPrice: String` | `commitmentTotalPriceString: String` | New. `null` for Android. |
| `billingPlanType: BillingPlanType` | `billingPlanType: String` (`"UP_FRONT"`, `"MONTHLY"`, `"UNKNOWN"`) | New. `null` for Android. |

Note that for 12mo commitment products, `InstallmentsInfo` is placed on `StoreProduct` instead of `SubscriptionOption`, since iOS doesn't have `SubscriptionOption`s.

### New `StoreProduct.identifier` Mapping
Previously, PHC's `StoreProduct.identifier` was built from `StoreProduct.productIdentifier` for iOS. Since `StoreProduct.productIdentifier` is just the product ID and doesn't contain the billing plan (like `com.rc.product:monthly`), this caused a bug when purchasing 12mo commitment products in the hybrids:
1. Fetch a 12mo commitment product (`com.rc.product:monthly`)
2. PHC returns a product with `identifier`: `com.rc.product`
3. Hybrid SDK calls PHC's `purchase(productID: String)` with `com.rc.product`
4. The native SDK would purchase the upfront billing plan instead of the monthly billing plan :(

This PR updates PHC to build `StoreProduct.productIdentifier` from iOS's new internal `StoreProduct.id`, which contains the billing plan's suffix.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes product identifiers and purchase lookup for iOS installment SKUs, which can break existing purchase flows if callers assumed base IDs; touches revenue-critical mapping across platforms.
> 
> **Overview**

items.title: iOS: `installmentsInfo` for Apple 12-month commitment billing plans is not mapped to hybrid SDKs
items.body:
### Summary

Apple's "Monthly Subscription with a 12-Month Commitment" billing plans are supported in `purchases-ios` 5.76.0+, but the data required to display them never reaches the hybrid SDKs. The docs acknowledge this — *"Available in the native iOS SDK in versions 5.76.0+, support in the hybrid SDKs is coming soon"* ([docs](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/subscription-guidance/apple-monthly-with-commitment)) — but I couldn't find a tracking issue in this repo, and this is where the mapping would live, so filing here.

RevenueCat/purchases-kmp#934 tracks the KMP-specific variant, but that has a different root cause (a pre-compiled `libRevenueCat.a` built with an older Swift toolchain) which does not apply to the CocoaPods-based hybrids.

### Current state

**The iOS mapper does not emit the field.** `ios/PurchasesHybridCommon/PurchasesHybridCommon/StoreProduct+HybridAdditions.swift` → `rc_dictionary` emits 17 keys, none installment- or commitment-related, even though `RevenueCat.StoreProduct` exposes `@objc public var installmentsInfo: InstallmentsInfo?`.

**Android does map it**, but onto a different type — `StoreProductMapper.kt` attaches `installmentsInfo` to `SubscriptionOption`, matching the Google Play model.

**The TypeScript types therefore only describe the Android shape.** In `@revenuecat/purchases-typescript-internal` (checked at 18.27.0):

- `PurchasesStoreProduct` has no `installmentsInfo` field at all
- `SubscriptionOption.installmentsInfo` exists, documented as *"Installment plans are only available for Google Play subscriptions"* / *"Currently only supported in Google Play"*

Since iOS products return `subscriptionOptions: null`, there is currently no place on an iOS product for this data to live.

### The two shapes aren't compatible

This is why it doesn't look like a one-line mapper addition — the existing hybrid `InstallmentsInfo` can't represent the iOS one:

| Hybrid / Android `InstallmentsInfo` | iOS `InstallmentsInfo` |
| --- | --- |
| `commitmentPaymentsCount` | `commitmentInstallmentsCount` |
| `renewalCommitmentPaymentsCount` | `commitmentInstallmentPeriod` |
| | `installmentBillingPrice` |
| | `installmentBillingDisplayPrice` |
| | `commitmentTotalPeriod` |
| | `commitmentTotalPrice` |
| | `commitmentTotalDisplayPrice` |
| | `billingPlanType` |

So this probably needs either a platform-tagged union, or `installmentsInfo` added to `PurchasesStoreProduct` with a superset shape.

### Why this blocks shipping

Apple requires both the monthly billing price and the total commitment amount to be shown before purchase is initiated. Through the hybrid bridge on iOS, neither is reliably reachable:

- `installmentBillingDisplayPrice` (the monthly amount) — not mapped at all.
- `commitmentTotalDisplayPrice` — only indirectly, since RevenueCat/purchases-ios#7299 makes `localizedPriceString` return it for commitment products. But there's no way to distinguish a commitment product from a regular annual one on the hybrid side, because `billingPlanType` isn't mapped either.

The practical effect is that an app rendering its own paywall in JS/Dart can't build a compliant one, even on an otherwise fully supported stack.

### Environment

- `react-native-purchases` 10.5.0 → `@revenuecat/purchases-typescript-internal` 18.26.0
- `PurchasesHybridCommon` 18.27.0 → `RevenueCat` 5.82.0 (≥ 5.76.0, so the native support is present)
- iOS 26.4+, Xcode 26.5+

Worth noting for scoping: the `#if compiler(>=6.3.2)` gate in `InstallmentsInfoFactory.swift` / `ProductsFetcherSK2.swift` should be satisfied for CocoaPods-based hybrids, since both `PurchasesHybridCommon.podspec` and `RevenueCat.podspec` build from source (`source_files`) in the consuming app's Xcode build. So unlike the KMP case, the native code path should already exist — the bridge mapping looks like the only missing piece.

### Ask

Is there a planned approach or rough timeline for the hybrid mapping, and is the intended shape a superset `InstallmentsInfo` on `PurchasesStoreProduct`? Happy to test a snapshot build, or open a PR if you can confirm the API shape you'd want.

items.title: feat(iOS): map Apple billing plan products (installmentsInfo) to the hybrid SDKs
items.body:
### Summary

Maps Apple's monthly billing plans with a commitment (`StoreProduct.installmentsInfo`, purchases-ios 5.76.0+) through the iOS bridge so hybrid SDKs can display and purchase them. Closes #1793.

Today the native support stops at the bridge: `rc_dictionary` never reads `installmentsInfo`, the product's `identifier` is the base StoreKit id, and `CommonFunctionality.product(with:)` cannot resolve a `{productId}:monthly` identifier. So an app rendering its own paywall from React Native or Capacitor cannot show the two amounts Apple requires before purchase (the monthly billing price and the total commitment), cannot tell a commitment product apart from the upfront product backed by the same StoreKit product, and gets `Couldn't find product.` from `purchaseStoreProduct`.

### Changes

**iOS (`StoreProduct+HybridAdditions.swift`)**
- `installmentsInfo`: new key, `null` unless the product represents a billing plan. Carries the iOS `InstallmentsInfo` fields (`commitmentInstallmentsCount`, `commitmentInstallmentPeriod`, `installmentBillingPrice`, `installmentBillingDisplayPrice`, `commitmentTotalPeriod`, `commitmentTotalPrice`, `commitmentTotalDisplayPrice`, `billingPlanType`). Periods use the same `{unit, value, iso8601}` shape Android emits for `Period`.
- `productPlanIdentifier`: new key (`"monthly"` for a billing plan product, `null` otherwise), the same key the `EntitlementInfo` and `SubscriptionInfo` mappers already emit, so a product can be joined to the entitlement it unlocks.
- `identifier`: now the compound identifier purchases-ios resolves the product by, `{productIdentifier}:{productPlanIdentifier}` for a billing plan product. Unchanged for every other product. This matches Android, where `identifier` is already `StoreProduct.id` (`{productId}:{basePlanId}`). `StoreProduct.id` is internal to purchases-ios, so the bridge rebuilds it from `productIdentifier` and `billingPlanType.rawValue`, mirroring `BillingPlanType.compoundProductIDPlanComponent` (`upFront` has no plan component).

**iOS (`CommonFunctionality.swift`)**
- `product(with:)` matches on the compound identifier. purchases-ios already resolves `annual:monthly` in `getProducts`, but the result's `productIdentifier` is `annual`, so the old filter dropped it and every purchase by product identifier failed for billing plan products. Package purchases were unaffected.

**TypeScript (`@revenuecat/purchases-typescript-internal`)**
- `PurchasesStoreProduct.productPlanIdentifier: string | null` and `PurchasesStoreProduct.installmentsInfo: BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo | null`, plus the `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo` interface and `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE` enum. The existing `InstallmentsInfo` on `SubscriptionOption` keeps Google Play's shape untouched. API report regenerated.

**Android and Web mappers**
- Emit `productPlanIdentifier: null` and `installmentsInfo: null` on the product, following the existing convention for the other platform's fields (`discounts` on Android, the `pricePer*` fields on iOS).

### Compatibility

- Purely additive for every product that is not a billing plan: `identifier` is unchanged, the two new keys are `null`.
- Billing plan products need purchases-ios 5.76.0+ (already the pinned 5.90.1), iOS 26.4+, StoreKit 2, and a build with Xcode 26.5+; on anything older `installmentsInfo` stays `null` exactly as `StoreProduct.installmentsInfo` does natively.
- No new source files, so no `project.pbxproj` change.

### Tests

- `StoreProduct+HybridAdditionsTests`: `null` fields and unchanged identifier for a plain product, updated key count, and a billing plan product mapped through `TestStoreProduct(installmentsInfo:)` covering the compound identifier, `productPlanIdentifier`, every `installmentsInfo` field, and the `upFront` case.
- `CommonFunctionality+PurchaseTests`: purchasing by `annual:monthly` resolves the billing plan product and reaches `purchase(product:)`. This test fails on `main`.
- The billing plan tests register only on an iOS 26.4+ runtime, since `StoreProduct.installmentsInfo` is unavailable below it.
- Android `StoreProductMapperTests`: key count and the two `null` entries.
- Web `offerings_mapper.test.ts`: the two `null` entries.

Run locally: TypeScript lint/test/build/api-extractor, web lint/test, Android `StoreProductMapperTests`, and the two iOS suites above on an iOS 26.5 simulator.

Also exercised end to end from a React Native app (react-native-purchases 10.10.0 with this branch swapped in by path, Xcode 27, iOS 26.5 simulator, StoreKit configuration file declaring a `MONTHLY` billing plan): `getProducts(['annual:monthly', 'annual'])` returned both products with the plan product carrying `identifier: "annual:monthly"`, `productPlanIdentifier: "monthly"` and a full `installmentsInfo`, and `purchaseStoreProduct` on it reached StoreKit with RevenueCat logging `Applying billing plan of type monthly to the purchase` (it failed with `Couldn't find product.` before the lookup fix).

### Naming

Open to renaming `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo` / `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE` or moving `installmentsInfo` under a different key if you would rather keep the Google `InstallmentsInfo` name free for a future unification; the wire shape is the part that matters for the hybrid SDKs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes product `identifier` semantics for iOS billing-plan SKUs and purchase lookup; purchase flows and paywalls keyed on the old base id could break for those products, though plain products stay unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Exposes **Apple billing plan products** (monthly billing with commitment, iOS 26.4+) through the hybrid bridge so React Native and similar SDKs can show required pricing and purchase by the right id.
> 
> On **iOS**, `StoreProduct` wire maps now emit **`productPlanIdentifier`** and **`installmentsInfo`** (commitment counts, periods, display prices, `billingPlanType`), and **`identifier`** becomes the compound id (`annual:monthly`) for plan products—aligned with Android’s `{productId}:{basePlanId}` shape. **`CommonFunctionality.product(with:)`** resolves products using that compound id so `purchaseStoreProduct` no longer fails with “Couldn't find product.” when the native `productIdentifier` is only the base StoreKit id.
> 
> **TypeScript** adds `BillingPlanInstallmentsInfo`, `BILLING_PLAN_TYPE`, and the new fields on `PurchasesStoreProduct` (API report updated). **Android** and **Web** mappers always send `productPlanIdentifier: null` and `installmentsInfo: null` for parity. Tests cover mapping, compound-id purchase, and null stubs on non-iOS platforms.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit faa697ecae4a070adedc5dff1e3b7b74cf60fe2d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Fix paid introductory price not mapped for Web Billing
items.body:
### Motivation

Web Billing products with a **paid** introductory price (e.g. $10 the first year, then $20/year) were reported by hybrid SDKs with `introPrice: null`. The API returns the intro price correctly, but the `purchases-js` hybrid offerings mapper dropped it.

### Summary

- `mapIntroPrice` only considered the free `trial` phase and hardcoded `price: 0`; it now falls back from `trial` to `introPrice` and uses the real amount.
- The subscription option's `introPhase` was hardcoded to `null` and the paid intro phase was missing from `pricingPhases`; both are now populated from `option.introPrice`.
- Precedence (`trial` before `introPrice`) matches the native Android mapper, so the two stay consistent.
- Added unit tests for a paid intro with no trial, and for the trial+intro case.

### Notes

Free-trial mapping is unchanged.

items.title: New Unified StoreReplacementMode APIs
items.body:
Introduces a new unified APIs for product changes that can be used across both the Galaxy and Play Store. 

## New APIs
This PR introduces two new typescript APIs:
### STORE_REPLACEMENT_MODE
```typescript
export enum STORE_REPLACEMENT_MODE {
    CHARGE_FULL_PRICE = "CHARGE_FULL_PRICE",
    CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE = "CHARGE_PRORATED_PRICE",
    DEFERRED = "DEFERRED",
    WITH_TIME_PRORATION = "WITH_TIME_PRORATION",
    WITHOUT_PRORATION = "WITHOUT_PRORATION"
}
```

### StoreProductChangeInfo
```typescript
export interface StoreProductChangeInfo {
    readonly oldProductIdentifier: string;
    readonly prorationMode?: STORE_REPLACEMENT_MODE;
}
```

The `STORE_REPLACEMENT_MODE` API matches the API found in the native Android SDK's `StoreReplacementMode`.

### PurchaseParams.productChangeInfo
```typescript
export interface PurchaseParams {
  // ...
  productChangeInfo?: StoreProductChangeInfo | null;
}
```

## Migration from .googleReplacementMode() to .storeReplacementMode()
The PR also migrates `common.kt` from using the now-deprecated `GoogleReplacementMode`/`PurchaseParams.Builder.googleReplacementMode()` APIs to instead use the new `StoreReplacementMode`/`PurchaseParams.Builder.replacementMode()` APIs from the native Android SDK.

If both a `googleReplacementMode` and a `storeReplacementMode` are provided, the `googleReplacementMode` is ignored and the `storeReplacementMode` is used.

## Tests
- Added plenty of unit tests for the changes in `common.kt`.
- Added API tests for the new purchase function variations in `common.kt`.
- Linked this branch into the RN SDK, and everything still compiled :)

## Other Notes
This PR intentionally does not deprecate the existing `GoogleProductChangeInfo`, `PRORATION_MODE`, or `PurchaseParams.googleProductChangeInfo` APIs, since we haven't yet introduced functions in the hybrid SDKs that consume the newly-introduced APIs. We will deprecate `GoogleProductChangeInfo`, `PRORATION_MODE`, and `PurchaseParams.googleProductChangeInfo` in a future PR once the new product change APIs are fully available.

items.title: Release/5.0.0
items.body:
**RevenueCat Purchases Hybrid Common v5** is here!! 😻

This latest release updates the Android SDK dependency from v5 to [v6](https://github.com/RevenueCat/purchases-android/releases/tag/6.0.0) to use BillingClient 5. This version of BillingClient brings an entire new subscription model which has resulted in large changes across the entire SDK.

### Migration Guides
- See [Android Native - 5.x to 6.x Migration](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/android-native-5x-to-6x-migration) for a more thorough explanation of the new Google subscription model announced with BillingClient 5 and how to take advantage of it in V6. This guide includes tips on product setup with the new model.

### New `SubscriptionOption` concept

#### Purchasing
In v4, a Google Play Android `Package` or `StoreProduct` represented a single purchaseable entity, and free trials or intro offers would automatically be applied to the purchase if the user was eligible.

Now, in Hybrid Common v5, an Google Play Android `Package` or `StoreProduct` represents a duration of a subscription and contains all the ways to purchase that duration -- any offers and its base plan. Each of these purchase options are `SubscriptionOption`s.
When passing a `Package` to `purchasePackage()` or `StoreProduct` to `purchaseStoreProduct()`, the SDK will use the following logic to choose which `SubscriptionOption` to purchase:
- Filters out offers with "rc-ignore-offer" tag
- Uses `SubscriptionOption` with the longest free trial or cheapest first phase
    - Only offers the user is eligible will be applied
- Falls back to base plan

For more control, purchase subscription options with the new `purchaseSubscriptionOption()` method.

#### Models

`StoreProduct` now has a few new properties use for Google Play Android:
- `defaultOption`
  - A subscription option that will automatically be applie when purchasing a `Package` or `StoreProduct`
- `subscriptionOptions`
  - A list of subscription options (could be null)

##### Subscription Option

Below is an example of what a subscription option:

```js
{
    "id": "basePlan",
    "storeProductId": "subId:basePlanId",
    "productId": "subId",
    "pricingPhases": [
        {
            "price": 0,
            "priceString": "FREE",
            "period": "P1M",
            "cycles": 1
        },
        {
            "price": 4.99,
            "priceString": "$4.99",
            "period": "P1M",
            "cycles": 0
        }
    ],
    "tags": ["free-offers"],
    "isBasePlan": false,
    "billingPeriod": {
        "periodUnit": "MONTH",
        "periodNumberOfUnits": 0
    },
    "isPrepaid": false,
    "fullPricePhase": {
        "price": 4.99,
        "priceString": "$4.99",
        "period": "P1M",
        "cycles": 0
    },
    "freePhase" {
        "price": 0,
        "priceString": "FREE",
        "period": "P1M",
        "cycles": 1
    },
    "introPhase": null
}
```

### Observer Mode

Observer mode is still supported in v5. Other than updating the SDK version, there are no changes required.

### Offline Entitlements

✨ With this new feature, even if our main and backup servers are down, the SDK can continue to process purchases. This is enabled transparently to the user, and when the servers come back online, the SDK automatically syncs the information so it can be visible in the dashboard.

### Offering Metadata

✨ Metadata allows attaching arbitrary information as key/value pairs to your Offering to control how to display your products inside your app. The metadata you configure in an Offering is available from the RevenueCat SDK. For example, you could use it to remotely configure strings on your paywall, or even URLs of images shown on the paywall.

See the [metadata documentation](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/offering-metadata) for more info!
